item.title: Why Congress is fighting over a central tool of American surveillance
item.summary: Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act is responsible for a huge share of intel collected by the U.S. Lawmakers and civil liberties advocates are worried it enables warrantless spying on U.S. citizens.

item.title: Israel and Lebanon set to meet for first direct talks in more than 30 years
item.summary: An official briefed on Israel's strategy for the talks described Tuesday's meeting as "preparatory" and aimed at laying out a framework for future negotiations.

item.title: Israel and Lebanon to hold first direct talks in decades
item.summary: Diplomats from Israel and Lebanon will meet in Washington for rare direct talks.

item.title: The labor economics of 'Alien' — and its lessons for inequality on Earth
item.summary: Behind the acid blood and jump scares of the Alien franchise is an even more insidious horror: a single employer with unchecked power. How Weyland-Yutani helps explain monopsony — and the rise of inequality on Earth.

item.title: In the brain, objects seen and imagined follow the same neural path
item.summary: New evidence finds that sight and imagination rely on the same neurons and use the same neural code.

item.title: 2 local TV giants merged. Then a court stepped in
item.summary: Local TV giant Nexstar's $6.2 billion deal to acquire rival Tegna won speedy approval from Trump administration regulators. But it faces a tough challenge from a pair of antitrust lawsuits.

item.title: Jesuit priest shares how Catholics are reacting to Trump's criticism of Pope Leo
item.summary: NPR speaks with Father James Martin, a Jesuit priest and author, about how Catholics are reacting to President Trump's recent criticism of Pope Leo.

item.title: U.K. inquiry lays bare 'catastrophic' missed chances before stabbings at dance class
item.summary: An inquiry found that a mass killing by a British teenager in 2024 at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class could have been prevented if his parents and state agencies had acted on his violence fixation.

item.title: Virginia joins a national effort to ensure only popular vote winners become president
item.summary: With Virginia on board, the National Popular Vote Compact is now enacted in states worth 222 electoral votes. Here's what that means.

item.title: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame's class of 2026 includes Phil Collins, Oasis and Sade
item.summary: The Rock Hall's inductees will include eight acts who have all been eligible for at least a decade. In its "musical influence" category, the hall nods to Latin and African pop for the first time.
